RESULT: `/work/putnam_2019_a5.lean` compiles with `lean /work/putnam_2019_a5.lean` and produces no errors and no warnings, including no "declaration uses `sorry`".

The only change to the file is the replacement of the single `sorry` with the tactic proof. The imports, the theorem statement, and `putnam_2019_a5_solution` are untouched. No axioms, `native_decide`, `#eval`, or metaprogramming were used. The scratch files I created have been removed.

The proof follows the standard argument, with `m = (p-1)/2`:

- **Divisibility criterion:** `(X-1)^n ∣ q` holds exactly when the Taylor coefficients of `q` at 1 vanish for all `j < n`. This uses `Polynomial.taylor`, and the coefficient at `j` equals `∑_{i<p} a_i · C(i,j)`.
- **Vanishing below `m`:** `C(i,j)·j!` is `descPochhammer` evaluated at `i`, so for `j < m` each power sum `∑ i^(m+d)` with `m+d < p-1` vanishes.
- **Nonvanishing at `m`:** the top term has exponent `2m = p-1`, and `∑ i^(p-1) = -1`, so the coefficient at `m` is nonzero. Hence `(X-1)^(m+1)` does not divide `q`.
